newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Record profits seen for POSCO in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Record profits seen for POSCO in 1997.

text.p: Higher sales prices and lower depreciation costs should push after-tax profits of South Korean steel giant Pohang Iron and Steel Co (POSCO) to record heights this year, company officials and analysts said on Monday.
Analysts said profits could be even higher, but added investors should be wary of POSCO's proposal to buy the assets of failed Hanbo Steel Co.
Oh Dong-ho, a POSCO accounting official, said POSCO's net profit would hit an historic high of 878.7 billion won ($988 million) on turnover of 9.08 trillion in calendar 1997.
"An increase in sales prices in the first half and sharply reduced depreciation will contribute to the surge," Oh said.
"We are quite sure we will meet the target."
Global steel demand would also increase as the steel industry would begin to recover after bottoming out in the first half of the year, Oh said.
Analysts were more optimistic than the company in their forecasts for POSCO's profits.
"The figures look achievable. Furthermore, POSCO's sales costs will be lowered due to the company's efficient operation," said Peter Lee, steel analyst at Dongbang Peregrine.
He estimated POSCO's profit would be 945 billion won, while a steel analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Capital Markets Ltd forecast 902 billion.
Kim Dong-jun, an analyst at Ssangyong Securities, was the most optimistic at 955.4 billion.
POSCO announced on Monday net profits of 543.23 billion won for the first six months of this year, up 40.8 percent from 385.83 billion won a year earlier.
Higher sales prices during the first half were cited as the major reason behind the increase in earnings.
Oh said the average sales price of POSCO's steel products was now 370,000 won per tonne, against 359,000 won previously.

For domestic hot-rolled sheets, POSCO raised its prices by 4.5 percent in April and 6.4 percent in July, analysts said. The company also increased its export price for hot-rolled sheet to $310 per tonne in the second quarter from $299 previously.
"Business itself has not showed any big improvements. But sharply falling depreciation did, which will contribute to the record profits," said Kim at Ssangyong Securities.
Analysts said depreciation would total 1.03 trillion won this year from 1.21 trillion last year.
But analysts were worried about POSCO's proposal to join with Dong Kuk Steel Mill to buy Hanbo's assets for two trillion won. Creditors so far have rejected the offer.
Moody's Investors Service said last week it had placed the A2 senior unsecured debt ratings of POSCO under review for possible downgrade because of its Hanbo proposal.
"The takeover is not helpful at all," said Lee at Dongbang Peregrine. "Additional trillions of won will be needed to complete the current Hanbo plant."
Analysts also said they worried about possible over-capacity in the steel industry in 1999 or in the year 2000 when Hanbo Steel would begin production.
The analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Capital Markets said Hanbo's COREX (core iron reduction exchange) was not a proven commercially viable technology.
"The takeover will not have a direct impact this year. But there are many uncertainties. It would be wiser for investors to take a wait-and see attitude," Kim at Ssangyong said.
Ssangyong recently downgraded POSCO to "hold" from "buy".
But Oh of POSCO defended the company's Hanbo plan.
"It can be negative news on the cost side. But it will not greatly affect our profit/loss structure," Oh said.
